title: Making Questions and No
summary: Learn how to make questions and negative sentences with do and does. You can talk about daily habits and routines.

sections.h: How to make negatives with do not and does not
sections.p: When you want to say no in the present simple, use do not or does not before the action word. Use do not (don't) with I, you, we, and they. Use does not (doesn't) with he, she, and it. Remember that the main action word stays simple, with no extra 's' at the end.

ex.en: I don't drink coffee in the morning.

ex.mean: Saying no about a third person

ex.en: We don't live in a big city.

sections.h: How to ask questions with do
sections.p: To ask a question about habits, put Do at the very beginning. Use Do with I, you, we, and they. Then add the subject and the action word. Keep the answer short and simple with yes or no.

sections.h: How to ask questions with does
sections.p: Use Does when you ask questions about he, she, or it. Put Does at the start of the sentence. Just like with negatives, the main action word does not need an 's' because the word does already shows it is he, she, or it.

ex.en: Does it rain a lot here?

words.mean: question word for I, you, we, they
question word for he, she, it

tip: Remember the helper rule: 'He, she, it' always likes the letter 's'. So use Does and Doesn't for them!
